title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 5o: dropping designs whose closed-form salt number r_kt is below -0.2, before any DFN run, kept the DFN-best design on 3 fresh pools and cut the 10-cycle screen's cost by 21 to 52%; 5n: ten DFN cycles plus a sqrt(cycle) fade fit found the best design to within 0.16% where the raw 10-cycle screen missed by up to 9.2%; 5m: a successive-halving ladder over resumed DFN runs
summary:
Milestone 5o (a salt floor before any simulation): drop every design whose closed-form salt number rkt (0.04 s per design) is below −0.2, then run 5n's union screen on the rest. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (192 PyBaMM runs, NCA_Kim2011@0.875×, Chen2020@1.75×, Ai2020@0.875×): it dropped 25 to 35 of 64 designs, returned the pool's DFN best on all three, and took 0.48 to 0.79 of the union screen's time (0.15 to 0.20 of all-DFN). The best design's rkt was never below −0.08 on 36 pools; a floor at 0 would have missed by 9.3%. The (energy, rkt) Pareto front is the wrong cut: on fade-limited Ai2020 the best sits on layers 4 to 7 and a 3-layer cut misses by up to 4.7%. Milestone 5n (late fade from ten cycles): DFN to cycle 10 on every design, a least-squares line in √cycle through cycles 5 to 10 read at cycle 100, and the top 4 by that extrapolation together with the top 4 by raw cycle-10 energy resumed to cycle 100. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (192 PyBaMM runs, Ai2020@0.275× and @0.35×, NCA_Kim2011@1.25×): within 0.16% of the pool's DFN best on all three, where the raw 10-cycle screen missed by 9.2% and 3.9%; the extrapolation lifted the low-current Ai2020 ranking from Spearman 0.10 and 0.48 to 0.57 and 0.63, and is anti-correlated on NCA_Kim2011 (−0.68), where the raw list carries the pool; wall time 0.24 to 0.32 of all-DFN (bar 0.30, mixed); against 5m's ladder 0.16% worse on one pool, 0.39% better on another. Over 33 conditions the union is exact on 29, worst 0.32%.

Milestone 5m (successive halving over resumed runs): DFN to cycle 10 on every design, then the top 16 resumed to 20, the top 8 to 50 and the top 3 to 100. Resuming (PyBaMM starting_solution, 10-cycle chunks) reproduces uninterrupted runs bit for bit on 23 designs at 0.85 to 0.97 of their time. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (216 PyBaMM runs, Ai2020@0.3× and @0.4375×, Ecker2015@0.75×): exact on two, 2.7% short on Ai2020@0.3× where the 10-cycle screen missed by 8.8%, at 0.24 to 0.29 of all-DFN’s wall time (a run’s first ten cycles cost 15 to 17% of it). There the best design ranks 28th of 53 at cycle 10 and first only at cycle 50: designs that start best fade fastest. Milestone 5l (retention from a short run): of the three factors of the 100-cycle score (thermodynamic energy, utilisation, retention), only retention needs simulation, and ten DFN cycles carry it. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (384 PyBaMM runs, Ai2020@0.625×, NCA_Kim2011@0.75×, OKane2022@1.75×): cycle-10 Wh/kg ranks cycle-100 Wh/kg at Spearman 0.92 to 0.97, and DFN@10 on all designs plus DFN@100 on the top 3 returned the DFN best on all three at 0.19 of all-DFN’s wall time; a sqrt-cycle fade extrapolation ranks worse. Known failure (development): Ai2020 at 0.25× and 0.375×, missed by 6 to 7%. Milestone 5j (salt pre-screen in the search) runs DFN, not SPMe, on every design whose closed-form salt ratio rkt is at most 0.10, and keeps the trust rule and band stop for the rest. Pre-registered on two fresh pools (256 PyBaMM runs, OKane2022 at 1.25× and Chen2020 at 1.5× current): it returned the DFN-best design on both, at 1.12× and 0.90× the earlier procedure’s wall time (median 1.01× over 19 committed conditions), so it is not a saving. It is a fix: on Chen2020@1.5× the earlier procedure stopped verifying inside the flagged block, one design short of the best (SPMe 19% low), and missed it by 4.5%. The best design’s rkt lay between −0.06 and +0.58 on all 21 conditions and below the flag on 8; discarding flagged designs would have missed by up to 17%, and a thermodynamic energy bound (never violated over 1,395 designs) prunes none of 429 flagged ones. Limits: two fresh conditions on graphite cells seen at other currents, one machine’s timings. Milestone 5i (closed-form trust flag) derives SPMe’s minimum salt ratio from the parameter set and the design alone: the steady electrolyte profile under SPMe’s uniform reaction, with concentration-dependent diffusivity handled exactly by the Kirchhoff transform. Pre-registered on the constant-diffusivity form over 1,280 committed designs (19 cell–current conditions): it ranks designs as SPMe does (Spearman 0.99) and predicts SPMe’s mis-scoring as well as the simulated flag (AUC 0.951 against 0.957), but over-predicts depletion (H66 mixed). The De(c) form, registered before 816 fresh PyBaMM runs were read, misclassifies 0 of 408 fresh designs (mean error 0.0003). It models SPMe’s electrolyte, not DFN’s (mean difference 0.03). Milestone 6a (measured cells) checks SPM, SPMe and DFN against the measured constant-current discharges PyBaMM ships for the Kokam cell of Ecker et al. (2015, 1C and 5C) and the Enertech pouch of Ai et al. (2020, 0.1C to 2C). Pre-registered: SPMe is never closer to the measured capacity than DFN by more than 0.13 points (H61 supported); where SPMe’s r_min is at least 0.5 the two agree within 0.06% while both miss the cell by 0.9 to 4.3% (H63 supported); r_min does not order the SPMe–DFN gap across the two cells (Spearman −0.14, H62 mixed). After the verdicts: the Ai cell’s logged temperature rise (1.6, 4.0, 10.4 K) matches PyBaMM’s lumped thermal model within 0.1 K; with heating the 2C SPMe–DFN gap falls from 1.50 to 0.32 points, and DFN’s 18.6 mV isothermal fit is heating error cancelling a 4% capacity offset. Default mesh, two cells, discharge only; no measured curve reaches the salt-starved designs where SPMe fails. Milestone 5h (a gap-aware answer step) targets 5g's one miss: on Ai2020 at half current SPMe scored nearly every sound design about 24% low, so the answer step stopped 3.2% short of the DFN best. The band stop keeps verifying with DFN while some unverified design's SPMe score times q (the median DFN/SPMe ratio over verified designs with r_min > 0.1, floored at 1) could beat the verified best. Chosen on the 13 committed conditions, it was pre-registered and run on six new ones with fresh designs (788 PyBaMM runs: Ai2020 at 0.75× and 0.25×, NCA_Kim2011, Chen2020 and Ecker2015 at 0.5×, OKane2022 at 1.5×). It returned the DFN best on all six at 0.33 to 1.07 of all-DFN wall time; 5g's iterate step did too, including Ai2020 at 0.75× where SPMe is 24% low (H58 refuted), so the band stop's extra 9 and 11 DFN runs on the Ai2020 pools bought nothing here. Over 19 conditions the iterate step misses on one (3.2%), the band stop on none. Rule recall stayed at or above 0.97; 13 Ai2020 DFN runs at 0.25× failed in the first cycle and were dropped. One PyBaMM version, 64 designs per condition, current the only condition varied. Milestone 5g (skip SPMe or not, at new currents) pre-registers a gate that reads the first 8 SPMe runs of a pool and skips SPMe (running DFN on every design) when 4 or more fail or deplete their salt (r_min ≤ 0.1), and otherwise runs the 5e rule with an answer step that keeps verifying the merged leader. It runs on 64 fresh designs at six conditions no run had used (768 PyBaMM runs): OKane2022, Chen2020, Marquis2019, Ecker2015 and Mohtat2020 at twice the areal current density, Ai2020 at half. Current moves the suspect share on every cell (Chen2020 0.25 to 0.81, Ecker2015 0.06 to 0.70, OKane2022 0.18 to 0.81, Ai2020 0.72 to 0.31 at half current). The gate chooses the cheaper branch on 4 of 6 (refuted): a structural SPMe failure costs under a second, so pools full of failures make SPMe cheap; the gated cost stays within 1.13× of the cheaper branch. The rule finds every mis-scored design at every condition. The answer is the DFN best on five conditions and 3.2% short on Ai2020 at half current, where SPMe scores designs a median 24% low and the best one is never verified (refuted). After the verdicts, a gate that also uses the SPMe-to-DFN time ratio from one DFN run is right on 12 of 13 conditions. Milestone 5f (a pilot switch and a verified answer step) tests, on 64 fresh designs on each of Mohtat2020, Ai2020, NCA_Kim2011 and Ecker2015 (515 runs), whether 8 SPMe runs plus 2 DFN runs can tell when to skip SPMe and run DFN on everything, and whether verifying the leading design until it is DFN-scored returns the DFN best. The answer step does, in all 120 replayed trials; all 3 early SPMe stops re-solve at tight tolerance to within 0.2% of DFN; recall stays 1.00. The switch fails its test: on Ai2020, where all-DFN is 11.6% cheaper, it fires in 20% of trials, because a salt cut-off of 0.10 misses mis-scored designs with minimum salt ratio up to 0.32. Across 11 cell pools the rule never costs more than 12% over all-DFN and saves 49 to 64% on six, so the recommendation is to run the rule every time. The switch constants were chosen on a post hoc replay of the seven committed cells. Milestone 5e (the rule on new cells) fixes in advance the two-part rule from 5c and 5d (re-solve early SPMe stops at tight tolerance; DFN-verify failed runs, then the rest in ascending minimum salt ratio, until three sound) and runs it on 64 fresh designs on each of two cells it was not built on, Marquis2019 and Chen2020 (256 runs). On Chen2020 it verifies all 9 mis-scored designs in 15 DFN runs (23% of the pool), among them the DFN-best design, which SPMe scores 23% low and ranks 16th; Marquis2019 has no mis-scored design and costs 4 runs. The planned answer step lands 1.3% below the DFN best on Marquis2019 because it compares verified DFN scores with SPMe scores that run 1 to 6% high at the top; taking the best verified design instead (chosen after the verdicts) reaches the DFN best on both cells. No run stopped early, so the re-solve step is untested. Milestone 5d (why SPMe fails) re-solves, pre-registered, every SPMe run on the committed benches that failed outright (61: NCA_Kim2011 49, OKane2022 12) or stopped early (6, Mohtat2020) under four solver and mesh variants, with 24 completed runs as controls (455 runs). Tight tolerances (rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, IDAKLU or CasADi) finish all 6 early stops, which then score within 0.3% of DFN; more Newton iterations finish none. No setting gives any of the 61 outright failures a usable score: in 59 SPMe’s linearised salt concentration goes below zero in the first discharge (median −8% of initial), the charge step has no valid start, and PyBaMM discards the run. So stops are re-solved, failures go to DFN. All four hypotheses supported; V0 reproduces all 91 committed runs. Milestone 5c (setting the cut-off on a new cell) compares, pre-registered, a trust-flag cut-off fitted to 8 random DFN runs with verifying designs in ascending order of SPMe’s minimum salt ratio until three sound ones in a row, on the three earlier cells and two new PyBaMM cells, Mohtat2020 and NCA_Kim2011 (64 Sobol designs each, 256 runs). On Mohtat2020 both fail (recall 0.00 and 0.17; H33, H34 and H37 refuted): its 6 mis-scored designs are SPMe runs whose solver stopped part-way (cycles 3 to 90), returned by PyBaMM as normal solutions, with no salt depletion. Among SPMe runs that finish, r_min ranks the mis-scored designs at AUC 0.995 or better on every cell that has any. Flagging early stops as well (post hoc), bottom-up verification finds every mis-scored design on all five cells with 16%, 95%, 6%, 14% and 88% of the pool sent to DFN (mis-scored shares 13%, 89%, 2%, 9%, 81%), always fewer than the 8-run calibration (23% to 98%). Milestone 5b (transfer) runs the trust flag and 9 frozen search methods, pre-registered, on two more PyBaMM parameter sets, Ecker2015 and Ai2020 (64 Sobol designs each, 384 runs, current scaled to the same areal density). SPMe's minimum salt ratio ranks the designs it mis-scores at AUC 0.995 on Ai2020 (57 of 64 mis-scored), but the OKane2022 cut-off r ≤ 0.07 misclassifies 20.3% there (best cut-off 0.33; H2 refuted); SPMe@10 no longer ranks DFN better than SPMe@100 (−0.01 and −0.11); the methods' ordering transfers (Spearman 0.73, 0.70), and the 2-cycle SPMe and DFN screens stay within 1.3× of the fastest method on all three cells while GP-EI is 1.9 to 3.7×. Cells are design-space variants (5% inactive rule, borrowed degradation parameters), not the published cells. Milestone 5a (fresh designs) re-tests, unchanged and pre-registered, the post-hoc winners of parts 2b and 4b on 128 new Sobol designs (384 PyBaMM runs, same parameter set). On pools of 64 the whole-pool 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best in 122.9 s against GP-EI's 220.4 s and the SPM@2 screen's 205.0 s (both p < 0.001); SPMe@10 ranks 100-cycle DFN at Spearman 0.668 against 0.575 for SPMe@100; the 15 methods' medians correlate at 0.924 across the two design sets. Cheap-start MF-UCB co-kriging beats GP-EI at every pool size but is 1.36× and 1.71× the best screen at 16 and 32 designs (refuted), and is fastest at 96. A 2- or 10-cycle SPMe screen stays within 1.4× of the fastest method at every pool size on both sets (descriptive). Same parameter set and protocol: transfer to other cells is untested. Milestone 3 part 2b (where SPMe errs) models SPMe's residual against 100-cycle DFN as a function of SPMe's own minimum salt ratio r. The registered form -ln r, from the log in SPMe's electrolyte overpotential, halves the cross-validated error (21.3 to 11.3 Wh/kg) and beats (1 − r)2 and the 0.1 flag. As a planner, fitted on 16-design pilots, it lands within 2× of SPMe's DFN cost on only 2 of 4 cycle counts. As an online correction it is slower than milestone 1's flag rule (528 against 418 s). Post hoc: SPMe@100's 14-call cost comes from the single DFN-best design, which is salt-depleted and drops from rank 1 at 10 cycles to 41 at 100. A plain whole-pool 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best in 123 s on pools of 64 and 172 s on 96, ahead of GP-EI (220 s) and every earlier screen. Exploratory: one parameter set, the same 128 designs. A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 4b (co-kriging multi-fidelity BO) replays autoregressive co-kriging over a cheap rung (SPM or 2-cycle DFN) and 100-cycle DFN, with augmented EI (Huang et al. 2006) and an MF-UCB fidelity rule (after Kandasamy et al. 2016), on the cached benchmark with measured run times. Started from five random DFN runs (122 s), no planned variant beats GP-EI (best 204.6 against 220.4 s on pools of 64; 267.1 against 220.4 s on 96) and all are far slower than whole-pool screening on small pools (157 against 46 s at 16 designs); three pre-registered hypotheses, two refuted. Charging each design its own measured time keeps the method order (Spearman 0.90). Exploratory, chosen after the result: starting from ten 2-cycle DFN runs ties the best screen at every pool size (38, 90, 144, 174 s at 16, 32, 64, 96 designs) and beats GP-EI at each. Milestone 3 (theory, part 2a) treats the screen’s residual as independent noise and gives an exact expected count of DFN runs (a one-dimensional integral for Gaussian noise). As a planner it calls whether whole-pool screening beats GP-EI right on 14 of 16 (screen, pool size) cases, against 8 of 16 for the worst-case formula; with one whole-space noise level it ranks the 11 screens only at Spearman 0.51 (refuted), 0.86 with the noise level near the top, because SPMe’s large errors fall on particular designs (on the DFN-best ones at 100 cycles: 14 DFN runs needed, 3 predicted). Milestone 3 (theory, part 1) proves that screen-then-verify needs at most as many full DFN runs as there are designs within 2κ of the best, where κ is the screen’s worst residual after the best affine fit, so scale and shift errors are free; the bound held on all 330 (screen, pool) cases. Across 11 screens κ ranks the DFN calls needed at Spearman 0.72, the raw error at −0.07; SPM’s residual is a quarter of SPMe’s (11.0 against 42.8 Wh/kg) and SPMe’s tracks its own minimum salt concentration (Spearman −0.82). The worst-case cost formula built on it predicted screen against GP-EI on only 8 of 16 pool sizes (refuted). Milestone 4 (search replay) replays 12 search methods on the cached benchmark, 30 pools of 64 designs, each simulation charged its measured wall time: screening every candidate with the plain SPM (100 cycles) or a 2-cycle DFN run and verifying in screen order reaches a design within 1% of the best 100-cycle DFN score in a median 153 or 160 s, against 220 s for GP-EI on DFN; the 10-cycle DFN screen takes 253 s (pre-registered H7, that it would need a third of GP-EI's time, refuted), successive halving over DFN cycles 247 s (185 s if runs resume), and milestone 1's trust flag cuts SPMe screening from 700 to 418 s. On pools of 96 GP-EI catches up, so whole-pool screening suits small candidate sets. Milestone 2 (dense benchmark) runs 128 fresh space-filling (Sobol) designs for 100 cycles under SPM, SPMe and DFN (384 runs, every cycle kept): a 10-cycle DFN run ranks the designs by their 100-cycle DFN Wh/kg at Spearman 0.962 (95% 0.932–0.977), against 0.641 (0.480–0.789) for a full 100-cycle SPMe run, at the same wall time (3.6 s against 3.7 s), and its top 10 contain the DFN-best design, which SPMe ranks 41st. Unplanned: the plain SPM ranks better than SPMe (0.955; 0.984 against 0.769 over the 121 designs SPMe completes), though it over-scores the best design by 20 Wh/kg, and 15 of 128 designs (12%) are mis-scored by SPMe by over 25%. Milestone 2a, the same question on the 49 stratified designs of energy-cell-dfn: 10-cycle DFN 0.977 against 0.834 for 100-cycle SPMe (paired bootstrap difference 0.138, 95% 0.057–0.271), and a linear fade extrapolation fails (Spearman 0.01). Milestone 1: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration classifies the designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 on the 49 (0.994 on the 128, whole-run minimum). Re-runs reproduce the committed SPMe and DFN scores exactly. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, costs timed on one design and one 4-core machine, no measured cell for these designs.
